title: SBA 7(a) vs SBA Express: The Short Answer
summary: SBA Express caps at $500K with a 50% guarantee and lender-made credit decisions. Standard 7(a) reaches $5M with up to a 75% SBA guarantee.
body_markdown:
SBA Express is a faster-decision delivery method inside the SBA 7(a) loan program. Standard 7(a), which covers loans of $350,001 to $5 million, carries an SBA guarantee of up to 75%. SBA Express caps at $500,000, carries a 50% guarantee, and lets the lender make the credit decision without SBA review.


Across most 7(a) programs, SBA guarantees up to 85% of loans of $150,000 or less and up to 75% above that. Either way, the SBA guarantees the loan and an approved lender funds it. Express also offers a revolving line of credit with terms up to 10 years, an option Standard 7(a) term loans don't provide.


For lenders, brokers, and embedded-finance platforms, SBA 7(a) vs SBA Express comes down to one trade-off: guarantee size versus who makes the decision. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA lender program details](https://www.sba.gov/sba-lenders/) confirm the caps: $5 million for most 7(a) loans and $500,000 for Express and Export Express.


### Side-by-Side Comparison Table


Both options sit under the same 7(a) umbrella, so many rules match. The differences show up in loan size, guarantee coverage, and who signs off on credit.


Feature Standard 7(a) SBA Express


Maximum loan amount $5 million $500,000


Maximum SBA guarantee Up to 75% (Standard 7(a) covers $350,001–$5 million) 50%


Who makes the credit decision SBA reviews, unless the lender has delegated authority The lender, under delegated authority


SBA review time 5–10 business days for SBA's own review None published; decision is lender-delegated


Revolving line of credit Not available as a Standard 7(a) term loan Yes, up to 10 years


Variable-rate maximums Base rate plus a capped spread by loan size Same caps


Eligible uses Real estate, working capital, refinancing business debt, equipment, furniture/fixtures/supplies, changes of ownership Generally the same 7(a) eligible uses, within the $500,000 cap


Personal guarantee Owners of 20% or more generally must guarantee Same rule


Best fit Larger amounts and borderline files that benefit from a higher guarantee Smaller needs and revolving working capital


One row deserves a correction. SBA's lender page lists review times for Standard 7(a) and 7(a) Small but none for Express. The widely repeated "36-hour" Express figure has no SBA source we could find, so confirm timelines with the lender.


### Loan Amounts and SBA Guarantee Percentages


The guarantee drives lender appetite. A higher guarantee means the SBA absorbs more of the loss if a borrower defaults, so the lender carries less risk.


- **Most 7(a) programs:** SBA guarantees up to 85% of loans of $150,000 or less and up to 75% above that.
- **Standard 7(a) amount:** Loans of $350,001 to $5 million, with SBA's maximum exposure at $3.75 million.
- **Standard 7(a) guarantee:** Every Standard 7(a) loan sits above $150,000, so the guarantee tops out at 75%.
- **SBA Express amount:** Loans and lines max out at $500,000.
- **SBA Express guarantee:** SBA guarantees 50%, regardless of loan size.
- **7(a) Small:** Term loans of $350,000 or less sit between the two, with the same 85%/75% guarantee tiers.


SBA guarantees 50% of an Express loan, so the lender keeps half the risk on every dollar. As a result, some lenders may apply a stricter credit box to Express files—plan for that when routing borderline applications.


Program rules shift often. Review Lendflow's summary of[2026 SBA program changes](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-loan-program-changes-2026) before you set credit policy or quote limits to borrowers.


### Approval Speed: Who Makes the Decision


Pre-qualified offers hosted on Lendflow drive an average of 42% faster speed to funding. That gain comes from the same lever that separates Standard 7(a) from Express: who decides, and how complete the file is when they do.


- **Standard 7(a):** SBA lists 5–10 business days for its own review of a Standard 7(a) loan.
- **7(a) Small:** SBA lists 2–10 business days for its review.
- **Delegated lenders:** Lenders with delegated authority skip SBA's prior review on eligible loans.
- **SBA Express:** SBA says Express lenders have "delegated authority to process, close, service, and liquidate the 7(a) loan without SBA review." SBA publishes no Express turnaround.


These figures cover SBA's review step only, not total time to funding. Treat any "36 hours" claim with caution, since speed under Express depends on the lender.


Lendflow's research on[SBA loan processing time](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-loan-processing-time-how-long-each-stage-really-takes) finds that most delays happen on the lender's side, so complete files and delegated lenders speed funding. Lender type matters too, according to the Federal Reserve Banks' 2025 Small Business Credit Survey.


About 21% of large-bank applicants and 16% of small-bank applicants reported a long wait for a credit decision or funding. Only 8% of online-lender applicants did, and these self-reported figures aren't SBA-specific.


### Interest Rates on Both Programs


The same SBA rate maximums apply to Standard 7(a) and Express. Variable rates are pegged to a base rate, either the prime rate or an optional peg rate, plus a maximum spread.


- **$50,000 or less:** Base rate plus 6.5%.
- **$50,001 to $250,000:** Base rate plus 6.0%.
- **$250,001 to $350,000:** Base rate plus 4.5%.
- **Greater than $350,000:** Base rate plus 3.0%.


These are ceilings. Rates may be fixed or variable, SBA publishes fixed-rate maximums separately, and the lender sets the actual rate within the caps.


Smaller loans allow wider spreads. A $40,000 Express line and a $40,000 Standard 7(a) loan face the same cap, so program choice alone won't change the rate ceiling.


### SBA Express as a Revolving Line of Credit


SBA Express supports revolving lines of credit with terms up to 10 years. Standard 7(a) permits revolving credit only under SBA Express, Export Express, or CAPLines.


A line beats a lump sum when cash needs rise and fall. Common fits include:


- **Seasonal swings:** Draw before peak season, then repay as revenue lands.
- **Receivables gaps:** Cover payroll and suppliers while waiting on customer payments.
- **Recurring working capital:** Fund inventory and operating costs without reapplying each time.


Lines of credit are one of the financing types Lendflow supports alongside SBA loans. Platforms can offer both from a single borrower flow and route each request to the right product.


### Qualification Requirements for Both


Standard 7(a) and Express share the same SBA eligibility baseline. The U.S. Small Business Administration lists its[SBA 7(a) eligibility requirements](https://www.sba.gov/loans/7a-loans/) as follows.


- **Operating business:** The business must be up and running.
- **For-profit:** The business must operate for profit.
- **U.S. location:** The business must be located in the United States.
- **Small size:** The business must be small under SBA size requirements.
- **Eligible type:** The business can't be an ineligible business type.
- **Credit elsewhere:** The business can't get the desired credit on reasonable terms from non-government sources.
- **Creditworthy:** The business must show a reasonable ability to repay.


Owners carry personal liability too. Under the Code of Federal Regulations'[13 CFR 120.160 guarantee rule](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-13/chapter-I/part-120/subpart-A/subject-group-ECFRa096ec067b9c6cf/section-120.160) , holders of at least a 20% ownership interest generally must guarantee the loan.


Lenders then add their own credit minimums on top of SBA rules. For Express, SBA's lender page notes that loans of $50,000 or less require no collateral.


Are SBA loans hard to get? The Federal Reserve Banks'[Fed Small Business Credit Survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/reports/survey/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms) found that about 32% of SBA loan or line applicants were fully approved. About 28% were partially approved, and 40% received no approval.


The 2025 survey, published in March 2026, uses a convenience sample of small employer firms. Its SBA figures cover all SBA loans and lines, not 7(a) or Express specifically.


A decline isn't the end of the file. Lendflow lets lenders build decline waterfalls—route a file declined for one product or lender to the next instead of letting it die.


### Refinancing Existing Debt and Merchant Cash Advances


Both Standard 7(a) and Express can refinance eligible business debt. Merchant cash advances (MCAs) follow stricter rules under SOP 50 10 8.1, effective October 1, 2026.


deBanked's coverage of the[new SBA MCA refinancing rules](https://debanked.com/2026/09/how-to-pay-off-an-mca-with-an-sba-under-the-new-rules-effective-oct-1/) quotes the SOP directly. An active sales-based repayment agreement isn't eligible for refinancing.


- **Conversion:** The original MCA must first convert to a term loan.
- **Amortization:** The converted loan must amortize for at least 24 months.
- **No new agreements:** No additional MCA agreements can be added after the conversion.


The prior SOP 50 10 8, effective June 1, 2025, barred MCA refinancing outright. Confirm details against the current SOP before you structure a deal, and see Lendflow's guide to[SOP 50 10 8 requirements](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sop-50-10-8-requirements-what-sba-lenders-need-to-know-in-2026) for lender-side context.


### How to Choose Between SBA 7(a) and SBA Express


Lenders and platforms route files across both programs by asking four questions. Borrowers can use the same filter before they apply.


- **How much do you need?** Anything above $500,000 requires Standard 7(a).
- **How fast, and who decides?** Express puts the credit decision with the lender, which skips SBA review.
- **Lump sum or revolving line?** Revolving needs point to Express, since Standard 7(a) term loans don't revolve.
- **How strong is the file?** Standard 7(a)'s guarantee of up to 75%, versus 50% on Express, leaves the lender less exposed on a borderline file.


Because Express caps at $500,000, larger real estate and acquisition deals will often need Standard 7(a). As a rule of thumb, smaller working capital or equipment needs can fit within the Express cap.


#### Other 7(a) Variations Worth Knowing


The 7(a) program includes more than two options. These variants can fit files that fall between Standard 7(a) and Express.


- **7(a) Small:** Term, non-revolving loans of $350,000 or less, with guarantees up to 85%/75%.
- **CAPLines:** Lines for seasonal, contract, building, or working capital needs, with a 10-year maximum maturity except Builders.
- **Export Express:** Loans up to $500,000, with a guarantee up to 90% on loans of $350,000 or less.


### Next Steps: How to Apply and What to Prepare


Lendflow's embedded finance customers operate with 80% smaller teams while converting similar funding volumes. Borrowers win too—Lendflow's research shows complete files and delegated lenders speed funding through either program.


- **Pick the program:** Match amount, speed, and structure to Standard 7(a) or Express.
- **Find a lender:** Choose a delegated or Express lender if speed matters most.
- **Assemble documents:** Gather every required form and financial record before you apply.
- **Submit a complete file:** Send every requested document together so the lender can move to a decision.


Express lenders mainly use their own forms plus SBA Form 1919. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA Form 1919 borrower form](https://legacy.sba.gov/document/sba-form-1919-borrower-information-form) is completed by the applicant and submitted to the SBA lender. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA Form 413 personal financial statement](https://legacy.sba.gov/document/sba-form-413-personal-financial-statement) is used to assess repayment ability and creditworthiness.

### Frequently Asked Questions


These answers cover the questions borrowers and lending teams ask most about SBA 7(a) vs SBA Express. Each answer reflects SBA rules as of November 2026.


#### What is the difference between an SBA 7(a) loan and an SBA Express loan?


SBA Express is a 7(a) delivery method where the lender makes the credit decision. Express caps at $500,000 with a 50% guarantee, while Standard 7(a) covers $350,001 to $5 million with up to a 75% guarantee.


#### What is the maximum SBA Express loan amount?


The maximum SBA Express loan amount is $500,000.


#### How fast is an SBA Express loan compared to a Standard 7(a)?


Express lenders decide under delegated authority, so there's no SBA review step. SBA lists 5–10 business days for its Standard 7(a) review and publishes no Express figure.


#### What is the current SBA 7(a) interest rate?


SBA sets maximums as a base rate plus a spread of 3.0% to 6.5%, depending on loan size. The lender sets the actual rate within those caps.


#### Are SBA 7(a) loans hard to get?


Per the Federal Reserve Banks' 2025 survey, about 32% of SBA loan or line applicants were fully approved and about 28% partially approved. Another 40% received no approval, and the convenience sample covers all SBA loans and lines, not 7(a) alone.


#### Can an SBA Express loan be a line of credit?


Yes, SBA Express supports revolving lines of credit with terms up to 10 years.


#### Do both programs require a personal guarantee?


Yes, owners holding at least 20% of the business generally must guarantee both Standard 7(a) and Express loans.


#### Can I refinance a merchant cash advance with an SBA loan?


Only after the MCA converts to a term loan and amortizes for at least 24 months under SOP 50 10 8.1. Active MCAs aren't eligible, so confirm details against the current SOP.
